title: Holy Spirit, Source of Gladness
description: Holy Spirit, Source of Gladness in Tonic Solfa to RUSTINGTON, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 483, “Come, Holy Spirit!”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens Double (8.7.8.7.8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to RUSTINGTON; any other Eights and Sevens Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ho-ly Spir-it, source of glad-ness, Shine a-mid the clouds of night; O'er our wea-ri-ness and sad-ness Breathe Thy life, and shed Thy light! Send us Thine il-lu-mi-na-tion, Ban-ish all our fears at length, Rest up-on this con-gre-ga-tion, Spir-it of un-fail-ing Strength!

lines: Shine amid the clouds of night;
Breathe Thy life, and shed Thy light!
Banish all our fears at length,
Let that love, which knows no measure,
Man can wish or God can send;

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1866.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to RUSTINGTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
